EXPLAINABLE & GOVERNED AI

Model method and decision boundaries

The objective is not to automate fraud determination. The capability strengthens preventive decision-making and routes higher-risk activity for proportionate review.

1

Receive existing controls

Consume approved rule results and events without changing the original operational systems.

2

Build behavioral context

Compare event frequency, sequence, relationships, and changes with historical patterns.

3

Detect anomalies

AI identifies unusual combinations that predefined rules may not capture. An anomaly is a risk signal, not proof of fraud.

4

Explain & recommend

Generate a behavioral risk score, confidence, reason codes, and a recommended route for specialist approval.

HUMAN-IN-THE-LOOP

AI suggestions never activate automatically

AI suggestion→Specialist review→Data & AI validation→GM approval→Activation
  • No automatic fraud confirmation, denial, payment suspension, or adverse action.
  • Only approved data and defined purposes may be used.
  • Missing or conflicting data lowers confidence and triggers human review.
  • Every assessment, route, override, and outcome is auditable.

AI AGENT CONTRACT

Behavioral Risk Decision-Support Agent

Human approval required
Goal

Create an explainable pre-action risk assessment and recommend a proportionate route.

Allowed

Read approved sandbox events, calculate scores, explain reasons, recommend routes, and propose indicators.

Not allowed

Change source rules, activate indicators, declare fraud, stop payment, or access unapproved data.

Human gate

Specialists approve case routing; Data & AI validates model changes; the GM is the final activation gate within delegated authority.

APPENDIX · SCORING METHODOLOGY

How the behavioral risk score is calculated

A transparent prototype method for committee review. Values shown here are synthetic Sandbox assumptions—not approved production policy.

Explainable by design
1

SOURCE-SYSTEM INPUT

Existing Control Score

Approved source-system rules produce or contribute to an aggregated score from 0–100. The prototype consumes that result without changing the original rule.

2

BEHAVIORAL AI

AI Anomaly Score

Each observed feature is compared with the synthetic historical baseline. Greater deviation contributes more of its approved maximum weight.

3

SEQUENCE CONTEXT

Pattern Adjustment

Additional controlled points apply only when approved combinations occur together—for example, a retroactive change within a rapid event sequence.

CURRENT SANDBOX CONFIGURATION

Combined assessment

55% Existing Control Score + 45% AI Anomaly Score + approved Pattern Adjustment

Worked example (70 × 55%) + (64 × 45%) + 8 = 75 Result: High risk → specialist review. The score prioritizes review; it does not confirm fraud.

ILLUSTRATIVE EXISTING CONTROLS

Different rules may carry different severity

These synthetic examples demonstrate the design only. Production severity requires domain approval and historical validation.

Illustrative rule result Prototype score Interpretation
Verified activity consistent with history 10 Low signal
Recent current-date exclusion change 50 Targeted verification
Repeated retroactive exclusion changes before request 70 Elevated control result
IBAN ownership mismatch across beneficiary profiles 88 Critical review signal

AI ANOMALY FEATURES

Maximum prototype contribution

A feature earns only part of its maximum when its deviation from the baseline is limited.

Rapid event velocity18 pts
Linked-entity concentration14 pts
Retroactive material change12 pts
Prior validated outcome12 pts
Identifier reuse: mobile, device or IBAN12 pts
Material amount or wage change12 pts
Cross-source conflict12 pts
Repeated control override8 pts

WHY AI MAY RAISE OR LOWER THE RESULT

Rules and behavior remain separately visible

If behavior is substantially more unusual than the existing control result, the AI strengthens the signal. If the observed behavior is materially less unusual, it may moderate the combined assessment. Neither component is hidden from the specialist.

DECISION BOUNDARIES

Configuration is governed

  • Low: 0–34 · Medium: 35–74 · High: 75–100 under current Sandbox assumptions.
  • An approved critical control can establish a minimum review floor.
  • Confidence is shown separately and is reduced by missing or conflicting data.
  • Specialist review, Data & AI validation, and authorized approval are required before activation.
